questions.q: Where were the genealogies of all Israel recorded?
questions.a: The genealogies were recorded on the scroll of the kings of Israel.

questions.q: Why was Judah carried away in exile to Babylon?
questions.a: Judah was carried away to Babylon because they disobeyed Yahweh.

questions.q: Who were the first people to resettle in their cities?
questions.a: The first to resettle in their cities were some Israelite priests, Levites, and temple servants.

questions.q: Which tribes did the people who resettled in Jerusalem come from?
questions.a: They came from the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh.

questions.q: Who was Uthai a descendant of?
questions.a: Uthai was a descendant of Perez, the son of Judah.

questions.q: Who was the firstborn son among the Shilonites who lived in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Asaiah was the firstborn son among the Shilonites.

questions.q: How many relatives of Zerah, including Jeuel, lived in Jerusalem?
questions.a: 690 relatives of Zerah, including Jeuel, lived in Jerusalem.

questions.q: Who were some of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Some of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem were Sallu, Ibneiah, Elah, and Meshullam.

questions.q: How many descendants of Benjamin lived in Jerusalem, according to their records?
questions.a: According to their records, 956 descendants of Benjamin lived in Jerusalem.

questions.q: Who were some of the priests who lived in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Some of the priests who lived in Jerusalem were Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin.

questions.q: For what was Azariah known?
questions.a: Azariah was the priest who was in charge of the house of God.

questions.q: Who were Adaiah and Maasai?
questions.a: Adaiah and Maasai were priests who lived in Jerusalem.

questions.q: For what were the relatives of Adaiah and Maasai known?
questions.a: They were very capable men in the work in the house of God.

questions.q: From which family of Levites was Shemaiah descended?
questions.a: Shemaiah was descended from Merari, one of the sons of Levi.

questions.q: Where did Berechiah live?
questions.a: Berechiah lived in one of the villages of the Netophathites.

questions.q: What responsibility do the gatekeepers carry out at the king’s gate?
questions.a: The gatekeepers stand guard at the king’s gate on the east side for the camp of Levi’s descendants.

questions.q: What was the responsibility of the Korahites?
questions.a: The Korahites guarded the entrances of the tent where Yahweh lived.

questions.q: Who used to be the leader over the gatekeepers, and who was with him?
questions.a: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, used to be the leader over the gatekeepers, and Yahweh was with him.

questions.q: What was the responsibility of Zechariah, son of Meshelemiah?
questions.a: Zechariah was the guard at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

questions.q: What did the gatekeepers and their children, whom David and Samuel placed into their positions of trust, do in Israel?
questions.a: The gatekeepers and their children guarded the gates of the house of Yahweh, the sacred tent.

questions.q: How often did the gatekeepers’ relatives come from their villages to help?
questions.a: Their relatives came from their villages to help for seven days at a time.

questions.q: How did the four leaders of the gatekeepers carry out their assigned task to guard the room and storerooms in the house of God?
questions.a: The four leaders of the gatekeepers would spend the night in their posts all around the house of God and then open it each morning.

questions.q: What specific tasks were the Levites assigned to do?
questions.a: Some of the Levites were in charge of the temple’s equipment and some were assigned to take care of the sanctuary utensils, and supplies like the flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.

questions.q: Who made the ointment from the spices?
questions.a: Some of the priests made the ointment from the spices.

questions.q: Who was responsible for making the flat cakes?
questions.a: Mattithiah, a Levite from the Korahite clan, was responsible for making the flat cakes.

questions.q: What was the responsibility of the Kohathites?
questions.a: The Kohathites were in charge of preparing the bread of the arrangement every Sabbath.

questions.q: Why did the singers and Levite family leaders live in rooms at the sanctuary when they were free from work?
questions.a: The singers and Levite family leaders lived at the sanctuary because they had to carry out their assigned tasks every day and night.

questions.q: Where did the leaders of the Levite families live?
questions.a: The leaders of the Levite families lived in Jerusalem.

questions.q: Who was the father of Gibeon, and what was his wife’s name?
questions.a: Jeiel was the father of Gibeon, and his wife’s name was Maacah.

questions.q: Who was Jeiel’s firstborn son?
questions.a: Jeiel’s firstborn son was Abdon.

questions.q: Who was Mikloth’s son, and where did his family live?
questions.a: Mikloth’s son was Shimeam, and his family lived in Jerusalem near their relatives.

questions.q: Who was Saul’s father, and who were Saul’s sons?
questions.a: Saul’s father was Kish, and Saul’s sons were Jonathan, Malchi Shua, Abinadab, and Esh Baal.

questions.q: Who was Jonathan’s son?
questions.a: Jonathan’s son was Merib Baal.

commentary.text: —This chapter expresses that one end of recording all these genealogies was, to direct the Jews, when they returned out of captivity, with whom to unite, and where to reside. Here is an account of the good state into which the affairs of religion were put, on the return from Babylon. Every one knew his charge. Work is likely to be done well when every one knows the duty of his place, and makes a business of it. God is the God of order. Thus was the temple a figure of the heavenly one, where they rest not day nor night from praising God, Re 4:8. Blessed be His name, believers there shall, not in turn, but all together, without interruption, praise him night and day: may the Lord make each of us fit for the inheritance of the saints in light.
